method: BioSPME 96-Pin Device (C18, ~80 nL coating) on a Hamilton Star robot + LC-MS/MS; empirical Freundlich isotherm fitted to bound against free concentration, log-transformed to a linear fit of log C_bound against log Cw. For PFBA, PFOA, PFHxS and PFOS the fit POOLS these data with the single-fibre C18-SPME data of Qin et al. 2023 (doi 10.1016/j.envint.2023.107857), which overlapped; for PFOS several low-concentration points were excluded
ka_units: log D_BSA/w at Cw = 1 umol/L (L_water per L_protein); Freundlich-type fit, NOT an association constant
protein_conc: 0.1-10 mg/mL BSA in PBS, chosen per compound to hold the bound fraction between 30 and 90%
ligand_conc_range: 9-step 2-fold dilution series
buffer: BSA in PBS, pH 7.4, 37 C, 250 rpm overnight
tk_relevance_noted: yes - the Freundlich slope IS the saturation: a linear sorption model assumes slope 0 and these are negative, so the apparent distribution ratio falls as the assay dose rises. Reprinted as SI Table S6 of the baseline-toxicity paper (doi 10.1021/acs.est.3c09950), where it supplies the protein term of that paper's mass-balance model

assay_volume_note: 600 uL aliquots in 96-deep-well plates (glass-coated for PFUnA, PFOSA, hexaflumuron and flubendiamide to limit sorption to plastic, plastic for the other 9); NO CELLS in this assay. buffer: human plasma diluted in PBS, pH 7.4, 37 C, 250 rpm overnight
tk_relevance_noted: yes - D_plasma/water offered directly as a PBTK input, and the paper's species result rests on it: PFBA, PFHxA, PFHpA, PFOA and PFHxS differ between trout and human plasma at LOW concentration and converge at high, because human plasma is protein-rich (42.25 vs 4.46 mL/L) so specific protein binding dominates there, while trout plasma carries proportionally more lipid (15.46 vs 7.08 mL/L) and lipid binding masks the specific term. The species difference is composition, not protein identity
